title: Release lifecycle orchestrator walkthrough — staged gates, A/B and rollback flows
creator: Marcus Nguyen
description: End-to-end walkthrough prototype for a Release Lifecycle Orchestrator feature in Redwood Console. Focus is on letting product/platform engineers author staged gates, create A/B/variant experiments, apply conditional traffic splits, preview rollout telemetry, and execute fast-rollback flows. Prototype emphasizes low-friction safe rollouts for model and route changes while surfacing cost and latency impact before commit.
acceptance_criteria: Designer prototype available in Figma that covers: create staged gate, define A/B variant, configure traffic split percentages, attach metrics and alert thresholds, run a dry-preview simulation, and trigger rollback
Interactive flow supports three safe-exit modes: immediate rollback, traffic ramp-down, and automated failover to fallback model variant
Preview panel displays estimated cost delta, 95th latency impact, error rate delta and expected token throughput for the proposed split
Usability feedback from at least two PMs and two engineers captured and addressed in follow-up iteration
Handoff notes include component library tokens, accessible color contrast for traffic lanes, and keyboard-first interactions for the timeline scrubber
design_decisions: Use a horizontal time-line scrubber for staged gates to make temporal sequencing visible without vertical scroll
Inline 'preview telemetry' panel to avoid modal context switches and provide immediate cost/latency estimates
Expose three rollback actions with descending severity: pause new traffic, re-route new traffic to fallback, full rollback to previous pinned model
Represent traffic splits as stacked area visuals with hover-to-breakdown for segment-level metrics rather than raw numbers to reduce cognitive load
Default to a conservative initial ramp (1%, 5%, 20%) when creating a new canary to encourage safe rollouts
tradeoffs: Showing rich telemetry inline increases cognitive density on the page; mitigated by progressive disclosure (collapse/expand) and concise microcopy
Implementing live dry-preview simulation requires backend sampling work (ENG-3321). Short-term we use synthetic estimates from historical distributions
Supporting arbitrarily nested conditional gates adds complexity to the UI; iteration 1 limits to linear staged gates and simple conditional pauses
Accessibility note: stacked area visuals are supplemented with numeric alt-readouts for screen readers, but visual identifiability between similar hues is constrained by product color palette

review_feedback: Sofia Patel (PM): Love the inline telemetry. Request to include cost projections by day and per-1000-requests estimate.
Mateo Rivera (Eng): Timeline scrubber is useful; need to ensure we can map scrubber points to stored rollout snapshots for audit logs (ENG-3999).
Priya Desai (Reliability): Add a 'safety fence' that prevents automatic ramp beyond configured thresholds without human confirmation.
Design lead (Ava Chen): Clarify visual affordances for which lanes are active vs shadowed; add clear labels for 'experiment' vs 'control' variants
ux_notes: Keyboard-first controls for timeline: left/right to nudge gate boundaries, shift+arrow for 10% traffic adjustments
Confirmation flows require typing the model alias when performing a full rollback to reduce accidental triggers
Microcopy for rollback actions includes expected downstream effects (cost, latency delta, SLO hit probability)
Provide a 'what-if' toggle that switches telemetry between 'historical-estimate' and 'synthetic-simulated' modes
